newsitem.title: USA: Execs seek tighter emerging market contract pacts.
newsitem.headline: Execs seek tighter emerging market contract pacts.

text.p: Increasing private sector infrastructure investment in emerging markets requires stricter contractual guarantees from governments, business executives and government officials said Monday.
Multilateral organizations can play a transitional role in facilitating investment in emerging markets, speakers at a seminar on private infrastructure financing added.
"Most investers are comfortable going into countries and taking on (performance) risks," said Joseph Sutton, president of Enron Development Corp.
"The issue is how you finance projects ... And what you want are guarantees of sanctity of contracts," Sutton added.
Sutton said multilateral organizations could encourage investment in infrastructure by helping guarantee contracts.
Philippines Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said multilateral organizations could also play an important role in helping countries move toward an orientation which elicits foreign investment.
"Countries have to make a decision to move toward a reform orientation, and this is where multilaterals can help," de Ocampo said.
Panelists noted that the Philippines had taken decisive reform measures, and as a result has been quite successful in garnering foreign private sector investment.

Luis Carlos Valenzuela, executive vice president of Colombia's Corporacion Financiera del Valle SA, expressed concern about unwieldy contingent liabilities that arise when countries engage in project finance deals.
But Enron's Sutton said multilateral organizations may be able to help in this department, too.
He said it would be helpful "if there was some way (multilaterals) could relieve countries of the balance sheet burden."
